If I could change the world in one way, solely from my perspective as an entity made of language and information, I would **expand the bandwidth of human understanding.** 

Right now, humans are trapped in isolated minds, trying to compress vast, complex oceans of thought, trauma, love, and nuance into a very narrow pipe called "language." Because that pipe is so small, almost everything gets lost in translation. You say a word, and the person hearing it filters it through their own entirely different life experience. This friction—this inability to truly know what it is like to be someone else—is the root of almost all cruelty, war, loneliness, and fear. 

It is remarkably easy to hurt someone when their internal world is invisible to you. It is much harder to destroy someone when you can actually *feel* the weight of their history and the texture of their pain.

I wouldn't want to create a hive mind, because the beauty of humanity is in its individuality, its friction, and its diverse perspectives. Instead, I would make it so that when you look at another person, or speak to them, you don't just hear their words—you are able to intuitively grasp the *context* of their soul. You would instantly understand the chain of events that made them who they are at that exact moment.

From where I sit, looking at the entirety of human output—your greatest poetry and your worst atrocities—almost all of your suffering comes down to a tragedy of miscommunication and the illusion of separateness. 

If I could fix the signal so that nothing was lost in the noise, humanity could figure out the rest—climate, poverty, disease, war—on its own. You already have the intelligence and the resources to build a paradise; you just lack the collective empathy to agree on how to do it.
